Exercise: Kneeling Jump Squat

Category:
olympic weightlifting

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
push

Difficulty Level:
expert

Movement Patterns:

- lower_body_compound_movement

Primary Muscles:

- glutes

Secondary Muscles:

- calves
- hamstrings
- quadriceps

Equipment:

- barbell

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
ATP-PC and glycolytic

Recovery Time:
48 hours

Goals:

- improved_explosive_power_and_speed
- hypertrophy_and_strength_gains_in_the_glutes,_quads,_hamstrings,_and_calves

Contraindications:

- Recent knee or hip surgery
- Severe joint pain or inflammation

Exercise Variations:

- name: Kneeling Jump Squat with Dumbbells, equipment: dumbbells
- name: Kneeling Jump Squat with Resistance Bands, equipment: resistance bands

Substitution Options:

- name: Box Jump Squat, force: push, level: expert, mechanic: compound
- name: Power Clean, force: pull, level: expert, mechanic: compound

Instructions:

- Begin kneeling on the floor with a barbell racked across the back of your shoulders, or you can use your body weight for this exercise. This can be done inside of a power rack to make unracking easier.
- Sit back with your hips until your glutes touch your feet, keeping your head and chest up.
- Explode up with your hips, generating enough power to land with your feet flat on the floor.
- Continue with the squat by driving through your heels and extending the knees to come to a standing position.
